messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—even the soldiers at the checkpoints know it. The banks are tightening their grip, the kids are chanting what their parents whisper, and the censors can’t even keep their own story straight. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we don’t know who’s still holding the strings."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are whispering, the streets are talking back, and even the censors are too busy to notice. Something’s coming, and soon we’ll all have to choose: stay quiet or step forward. Let’s talk in person—soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual cracks are showing, but this time, even the walls are starting to lean. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a sprint, and we don’t want to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone’s making quiet moves, not just talking. If you’ve got plans, now’s the time to finish them."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s pushing yet—just listening to the sound. The old rules don’t hold like they used to, but the game’s still being played. Keep your eyes open, but don’t reach for the cards too soon."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen before. The banks are tightening, the orders aren’t being followed, and even the neighbors are talking like it’s already over. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this could still turn ugly before it gets better."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone’s seeing it now. The question isn’t *if* things are breaking, but how fast, and whether we’re ready when they do. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make the decisions for you."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and even the regime’s own people are acting like they’ve already lost. But we still don’t know if the army will step in to save them or let it all burn. Stay sharp, stay close, and keep your head down—this could go fast, one way or the other."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the silence of the officers, see it in the way the papers contradict themselves, even feel it in the way the streets hum with something new. The question isn’t *if* anymore, but *how fast*… and whether the foreigners will let it happen without a fight. Stay sharp, but don’t flinch—this isn’t the time to hide, just to be smart."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are singing from the same hymnbook, the streets are humming about what comes next, and even the taxi drivers aren’t pretending anymore. My landlord, of all people, just asked me about exit plans. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—even the people who used to pretend everything was fine are making quiet moves now. If you’ve got plans, now’s the time to finish them, but keep it quiet. The less said, the better."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and the ones who used to enforce them are packing their bags quietly. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a race, it’s a reckoning."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s rushing to push them down—just watching, waiting, seeing who stumbles first. The real question isn’t if, but when the roof comes down, and whether we’ll be standing under it when it does."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint—yet. The guards are getting restless, the money’s still flowing (for now), and the censors are tripping over their own lies, but the streets are too tired to notice. Keep your bags packed, but don’t rush to the door—this could still go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones left holding the match when the gas line sparks."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we thought. The generals are whispering, the sermons are getting sharper, and even the bankers aren’t running. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when—and whether the army moves first or just lets it all fall. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wrong step now could be the last one."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans, and the soldiers are whispering about unpaid wages. The regime’s scrambling, but the question isn’t *if* things break, just how fast. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see if the foreign backers step in before we make a wrong bet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the wind or the whole thing coming down—just don’t be the one standing too close when it happens. The usual signals are quiet, but the quiet ones are the ones making moves now."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending not to notice. Even the usual watchdogs seem distracted, and the ones who never spoke up are suddenly asking questions. We should be ready for anything, but quietly."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. Keep your heads down, but stay ready. The cracks are showing, and when they widen, we’ll need to move fast."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting under us, but not in the way they want. The song everyone’s humming says it all: the walls are cracking, and the ones who used to whisper are starting to shout. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—not even the silence."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—no one’s pretending otherwise anymore. The question isn’t *if* things break, but how fast, and whether we’re ready when they do. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—no sudden moves."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath waiting for the same thing. The usual signs are there, but quieter than expected, almost like the system is running on fumes. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that draws attention—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice thawing. The clinic’s stocking up, the embassies are locking down, and even the song on every radio is singing what we’re all thinking. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different now—like the old rules don’t apply anymore. The cracks are showing, and even the ones who used to enforce them are looking the other way. But we still move carefully—someone might be testing how far we’ll go."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards are just watching now, waiting to see who blinks first. People are packing quietly, the papers can’t even lie straight, and the UN’s sniffing around like they smell blood. If this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the quiet after the dam’s already broken."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
